Q21.question: Define Supervised Learning.
Q21.reference_answer: A type of ML where the model is trained on labeled data with known inputs and outputs.

rubric.text: Supervised learning is a type of machine learning in which the model is trained on labeled data.
The labeled training data contains inputs together with their known correct outputs.

Q22.question: Evaluation Case Study: A model (M1) achieves 99% accuracy on the training set but only 30% accuracy on the testing set. What is happening to this model?
Q22.reference_answer: Overfitting; the model has memorized the training data but failed to generalize.

rubric.text: Model M1 is overfitting, because it scores 99% on training data but only 30% on test data.
The model has memorized the training data and fails to generalize to unseen data.

Q23.question: What is Regression Analysis?
Q23.reference_answer: A statistical process for estimating the relationships between a dependent variable and one or more independent variables.

rubric.text: Regression analysis is a statistical process for estimating the relationship between variables.
It relates a dependent variable to one or more independent variables.

Q24.question: List and elucidate two major challenges in Machine Learning.
Q24.reference_answer: Data quality/missing values, overfitting/underfitting, data collection, or time consumption.

rubric.text: Poor data quality, missing values or difficulty in collecting data is a major challenge in machine learning.
Overfitting, underfitting or the long time needed to train models is a major challenge in machine learning.

Q25.question: List any two major real-world applications of Data Science.
Q25.reference_answer: Healthcare/disease prediction, Finance/fraud detection, E-commerce recommendation systems.

rubric.text: Healthcare, such as disease prediction, is a major real-world application of data science.
Finance fraud detection or e-commerce recommendation systems are major applications of data science.

Q26.question: Distinguish between Structured and Semi-structured data.
Q26.reference_answer: Structured is organized in rows/columns (SQL, Excel); Semi-structured has some markers but isn't in a grid (JSON, XML, HTML).

rubric.text: Structured data is organized in rows and columns, as in SQL tables or Excel sheets.
Semi-structured data has some tags or markers but is not in a grid, as in JSON, XML or HTML.

Q27.question: Describe methods used to detect and handle outliers in a dataset.
Q27.reference_answer: Detection: Z-score, IQR, Scatter plots, Box plots. Handling: Trimming, Capping, or Imputation.

rubric.text: Outliers can be detected with the Z-score, the IQR rule, scatter plots or box plots.
Outliers can be handled by trimming them, capping them or imputing new values.

Q28.question: What is Data Pre-processing?
Q28.reference_answer: The steps taken to clean and transform raw data into a format suitable for a machine learning model.

rubric.text: Data pre-processing is the set of steps that clean the raw data.
Pre-processing transforms raw data into a format suitable for a machine learning model.

Q29.question: Why is Data Normalization required for the K-Nearest Neighbors (K-NN) algorithm?
Q29.reference_answer: K-NN is distance-based; features with larger scales will dominate the distance calculation if not normalized.

rubric.text: K-NN is a distance-based algorithm that compares data points by their distance.
Without normalization, features with larger scales dominate the distance calculation.

Q30.question: How are continuous attributes discretized? Give an example.
Q30.reference_answer: By grouping values into bins or intervals, e.g., turning ages 1-100 into 'Child,' 'Adult,' 'Senior.'

rubric.text: Continuous attributes are discretized by grouping their values into bins or intervals.
For example, ages from 1 to 100 can be grouped into child, adult and senior bins.

Q31.question: What does the 'K' represent in the K-Means clustering algorithm?
Q31.reference_answer: The predefined number of clusters or groups the data will be divided into.

rubric.text: K is the number of clusters that the data is divided into by K-Means.
The number of clusters K is predefined, chosen before the algorithm runs.

Q32.question: Name three common Hyperparameters in Machine Learning algorithms.
Q32.reference_answer: K in K-NN, Learning Rate, Number of Estimators/Trees, Max Depth, or Batch Size.

rubric.text: K in K-NN, the maximum tree depth or the number of trees are hyperparameters of machine learning algorithms.
The learning rate and the batch size are hyperparameters of machine learning algorithms.

Q33.question: Define Gradient Descent.
Q33.reference_answer: An optimization algorithm used to minimize the cost function by iteratively moving toward the steepest descent.

rubric.text: Gradient descent is an optimization algorithm that minimizes a cost function.
Gradient descent iteratively updates the parameters by moving in the direction of steepest descent.

Q34.question: Classifier Comparison: Compare three SVM classifiers based on their margins and boundaries.
Q34.reference_answer: Discussion on maximizing the margin and ensuring no data points fall within the 'gutter' or margin.

rubric.text: The best SVM classifier is the one with the widest margin between the boundaries.
A good classifier has no data points falling inside the margin and no misclassified points.

Q35.question: Explain how the Radial Basis Function (RBF) Kernel works in SVM.
Q35.reference_answer: It transforms data into a higher-dimensional space to find a non-linear decision boundary.

rubric.text: The RBF kernel maps the data into a higher-dimensional space.
This lets the SVM find a non-linear decision boundary.
